message.content:
**Proteins that are found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often serve as channels, transporters, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., **β‑adrenergic receptor**, **rhodopsin**
• **Ionotropic glutamate receptors** (e.g., **NMDA receptor**) | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via electrostatic interactions or lipid anchors; often involved in signaling or cytoskeletal linkage. | • **Ankyrin‑B** (links integral proteins to the spectrin-actin cytoskeleton)
• **Spectrin** (provides structural support)
• **Actin** (interacts with membrane proteins via ERM proteins)
• **Src family kinases** (e.g., **c‑Src**) – attach to the inner leaflet and phosphorylate membrane proteins | | **Glycoproteins / Glycolipids** | Often serve as cell‑surface markers or adhesion molecules. | • **CD45** (protein tyrosine phosphatase on leukocytes)
• **E‑cadherin** (cell‑cell adhesion)
• **Integrin α5β1** (extracellular matrix binding) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to lipids (e.g., farnesyl, geranylgeranyl, or GPI anchors). | • **GPI‑anchored CD59** (protects cells from complement)
• **Ras** (farnesylated GTPase) | | **Transporters & Channels** | Mediate selective movement of ions or molecules. | • **Voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv1.2)**
• **Calcium‑activated chloride channel (TMEM16A)**
• **Sodium‑glucose cotransporter (SGLT1)** | ### How to think about them 1. **Integral proteins** are embedded in the lipid bilayer and usually have one or more transmembrane helices. 2. **Peripheral proteins** sit on the cytoplasmic or extracellular side and can be released by altering ionic strength or pH. 3. **Lipid‑anchored proteins** are tethered to the membrane via a lipid moiety rather than spanning it. 4. **Glycoproteins** carry carbohydrate chains that can mediate cell‑cell recognition. These proteins together give the plasma membrane its functional diversity—allowing cells to sense their environment, transport nutrients, maintain ion gradients, and communicate with other cells.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?" They want a list of proteins found in the plasma membrane. We can provide a general answer: types of proteins: integral membrane proteins (e.g., ion channels, transporters, receptors), peripheral membrane proteins (e.g., cytoskeletal proteins, signaling proteins). Provide examples: e.g., Na+/K+ ATPase, GLUT1, G-protein coupled receptors like rhodopsin, integrins, cadherins, etc. Also mention peripheral proteins like ankyrin, spectrin, actin-binding proteins. Provide categories and examples. No function call needed.
